subject: general
question: In the Fixed Exchange Rate system, the _________ fixes the exchange rates at a particular level.
solution:
The correct answer is __**government**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In the Fixed Exchange Rate System**, **the government fixes **the exchange rates at a particular level. 
 
• A fixed exchange rate is a system used **by a government or central bank **that links the value of the** nation's official currency to the currency of another nation or the price of gold.**
 
• A fixed exchange rate system's goal is to maintain a currency's value within a specific range.
 
• **Fixed exchange **rates assist the government to** maintain low inflation and provide exporters and importers more security.**
 
• In the early 1970s, the floating exchange rate system was adopted by several industrialized countries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **For importers and exporters,** fixed rates increase predictability.
 
• **Fixed rates **also assist the government in maintaining low inflation, which over time helps to keep interest rates low and promotes investment and commerce.
 
• The majority of large industrialized countries have had floating exchange rate systems, where the price of a currency is determined by the global market rate (forex).
